title: USCIS to Revise I-539 and I-765 Forms Starting September 15
excerpt: New changes impact visa applications for H-1B families and international students.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • USCIS revises I-539 and I-765 forms effective September 15, 2026.
  • New requirements may complicate applications for H-1B families.
  • International students face additional documentation for work authorization.
  • Changes impact thousands of Indian families and students in the U.S.
  • Preparation is essential for navigating the revised application process.

Changes to I-539 and I-765 Forms

The U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is set to implement changes to the I-539 and I-765 forms on September 15, 2026. These forms are crucial for various visa applications, particularly for H-1B visa holders and their dependents, as well as international students seeking work authorization. The revisions aim to streamline the application process and improve clarity, but they also introduce new requirements that applicants must navigate.

Impact on H-1B Families

The I-539 form is primarily used by individuals applying for a change of status or extending their stay in the U.S. This form is essential for H-1B visa holders who wish to apply for dependent visas for their spouses and children. With the upcoming changes, applicants will need to provide additional documentation to demonstrate their eligibility. This could include proof of financial support and more detailed information about the applicant's current status.

Families of H-1B visa holders should prepare for these changes by reviewing their current documentation and ensuring they meet the new requirements. The USCIS has indicated that the updates are designed to reduce processing times, but applicants may experience delays as the agency adjusts to the new system.

International Students and Work Authorization

The I-765 form is used by international students to apply for work authorization, particularly for Optional Practical Training (OPT) and Curricular Practical Training (CPT). The revisions to this form will require students to provide more comprehensive information about their academic programs and any prior employment history in the U.S. This change is intended to enhance the integrity of the work authorization process, but it may also complicate applications for students who are already facing challenges in securing employment.

International students should familiarize themselves with the new requirements and consider seeking guidance from their university's international student office. With the job market becoming increasingly competitive, understanding these changes will be crucial for students looking to maximize their opportunities in the U.S.

Broader Implications for the Indian Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, these changes are particularly significant. India is one of the largest sources of H-1B visa holders and international students in the U.S. The updated forms could affect thousands of Indian families and students who rely on these pathways for education and employment opportunities in the U.S. The Indian community has a vested interest in monitoring these changes, as they could influence future immigration policies and the overall landscape for skilled workers in the U.S.

As the USCIS rolls out these changes, it will be essential for applicants to stay informed and prepared. Engaging with immigration attorneys or advocacy groups may provide additional support in navigating the complexities of the new forms.

Conclusion

The USCIS's revisions to the I-539 and I-765 forms represent a significant shift in the application process for many visa holders and international students. While the agency aims to streamline procedures, the added requirements may pose challenges for applicants. As the September 15 deadline approaches, it is crucial for affected individuals to understand the implications of these changes and prepare accordingly.
